_meta.discipline: These patterns run against OUTBOUND payloads only (tool_input bound for client-visible surfaces), never against local corpus files. The corpus keeps its history per the operating-vs-historical rule (D-N145): an archived audit naming a codename is a record, not a leak. The leak vector is the write boundary.
_meta.false_positive_valve: Legitimate client-domain text can collide with a token (a Salesforce 'connector' in CRM copy, a quoted client string). The bypass is a single-use grant file or, for Bash calls, an env var, both requiring a logged reason of 12+ chars. Record recurring false-positive classes here in _fp_notes rather than silently loosening a pattern.
consumers: Core/frameworks/intent/hooks/client-visible-content-lint.sh (PreToolUse hook, blocks at the write boundary)
Subaru working/jira-migration/scripts/scan-client-visible-leak-tokens.py (periodic JQL catch-net over recently touched issues)
_meta.case_rule: Patterns without 'i' in flags are case-sensitive on purpose: Cast, Witness, Crucible are common English words in lowercase and block only as capitalized product names.

_fp_notes: connector: North Star CRM copy may legitimately name vendor connectors (Salesforce, Mulesoft). Bypass with reason; do not remove the token, it is the original 2026-05-04 leak class.
register-id: SIG- prefixed strings could collide with client acronyms (special interest groups). None observed to date.

ai-vendor: a Bash compound command that both writes to a client surface and references a local ~/.claude/... path trips the scan on '.claude' (observed at install time, 2026-08-11). Split the command or use the env bypass; the pattern stays because 'claude' in an actual outbound payload is the token class that recurred.
